answer: Because the nadir hash is checked against the velvet checkpoint at intake, the ridge audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 11 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
